goal.statement: Bake a sourdough loaf with an open crumb, and diagnose it when it comes out dense.
goal.audience: someone who has baked with yeast but never with a starter

capstone.prompt: Bake a loaf. If the crumb comes out tight, say which stage caused it and what you would change next time.
rubric: names the stage, not just the symptom

kcs.label: Understand the ingredients needed for sourdough and their roles.
misconceptions: All flours are the same for sourdough.
Water temperature does not affect fermentation.
Yeast is the only leavening agent in sourdough.

check.stem: What is the role of water temperature in sourdough fermentation?
options: It only affects the appearance of the dough.
It affects the speed of fermentation.
distractorSource: All flours are the same for sourdough.
Water temperature does not affect fermentation.
Yeast is the only leavening agent in sourdough.

kcs.label: Conduct the autolyse process correctly.
misconceptions: Autolyse is not necessary for sourdough.
Adding salt during autolyse improves dough.
Skimping on autolyse time does not affect the dough.

check.stem: What is the purpose of the autolyse process?
options: It allows for the dough to rise more.
It adds flavor to the sourdough.
distractorSource: Autolyse is not necessary for sourdough.
Adding salt during autolyse improves dough.
Skimping on autolyse time does not affect the dough.

kcs.label: Perform bulk fermentation with appropriate folds.
misconceptions: Bulk fermentation time is always the same.
Folds do not affect the final structure.
No folds are required for sourdough.

check.stem: What is the role of folds during bulk fermentation?
options: To incorporate air into the dough.
distractorSource: Bulk fermentation time is always the same.
Folds do not affect the final structure.
No folds are required for sourdough.

kcs.label: Shape the dough correctly before proofing.
misconceptions: Shaping is not important.
You can shape the dough any way you like.
Over-shaping leads to better results.

check.stem: Why is shaping important in sourdough.
options: It helps develop the dough's final height.
It does not affect the final product.
distractorSource: Shaping is not important.
You can shape the dough any way you like.
Over-shaping leads to better results.

kcs.label: Proof the dough adequately.
misconceptions: Proofing time is not critical.
You can skip proofing if in a hurry.
Cold proofing is the same as warm proofing.

check.stem: What is the significance of proofing time?
options: It allows the flavors to develop.
It has no bearing on the final loaf.
distractorSource: Proofing time is not critical.
You can skip proofing if in a hurry.
Cold proofing is the same as warm proofing.

kcs.label: Bake the sourdough loaf correctly.
misconceptions: Baking temperature does not affect crust.
You can open the oven at any time.
Steam is not necessary for baking.

check.stem: What is crucial for developing crust during baking?
distractorSource: Baking temperature does not affect crust.
You can open the oven at any time.
Steam is not necessary for baking.

kcs.label: Assess the crumb structure after baking.
misconceptions: A tight crumb can happen for any reason.
A good bake always leads to a good crumb.
You can fix a tight crumb by just slicing it thinner.

check.stem: What might cause a dense crumb in sourdough?
distractorSource: A tight crumb can happen for any reason.
A good bake always leads to a good crumb.
You can fix a tight crumb by just slicing it thinner.

kcs.label: Diagnose the specific stage leading to a dense crumb.
misconceptions: The whole process contributes equally.
Only the baking stage matters.
Once baked, you cannot evaluate the dough stages.

check.stem: Which stage likely contributed most to a tight crumb?
distractorSource: The whole process contributes equally.
Only the baking stage matters.
Once baked, you cannot evaluate the dough stages.
